news.headline: uniQure submits US BLA and UK MAA for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease
news.summary: uniQure filed a Biologics License Application with the FDA seeking accelerated approval for ifezuntirgene inilparvovec (AMT-130) and, in parallel, a Marketing Authorisation Application with the UK MHRA, both supported by the three-year Phase I/II analysis versus a propensity-score-matched Enroll-HD external control. The company requested priority review, which would compress the FDA review to six months after the 60-day filing review, and reiterated that it intends to present the four-year Phase I/II analysis before the end of Q3 2026.

news.headline: Reuters: uniQure seeks US approval for Huntington's gene therapy after FDA reversal
news.summary: Reuters framed the filing as the payoff from the FDA's June 2026 reversal, when the agency agreed to accept the existing Phase I/II data for accelerated review after previously demanding a new randomized trial with a placebo-surgery arm. Priority review, if granted, would cut the review clock to six months from the standard ten; the earlier dispute ran during the tenure of gene-therapy chief Vinay Prasad, who left the FDA in April 2026.

news.headline: William Blair resumes coverage at Outperform with $73 value as the stock round-trips the filing pop
news.summary: Analyst Sami Corwin resumed coverage with an Outperform rating and a $73 sum-of-the-parts value, roughly 58% above the post-filing price, calling FDA acceptance of the BLA the next incremental de-risking event and approval itself the substantial one; William Blair models peak global AMT-130 sales of about $3.2B in 2035 and sees approval in two countries during 2027. Shares nonetheless sold the news, spiking to an intraday $50.74 on September 3 before closing at $45.49.

news.headline: ICER opens a cost-effectiveness review of AMT-130 with a March 2027 CEPAC meeting
news.summary: The Institute for Clinical and Economic Review launched an assessment of AMT-130, with public comment on the draft scoping document open until September 11, 2026 and a revised scoping document due on or about September 21, 2026. The Midwest CEPAC will publicly deliberate and vote on the evidence in March 2027, making this the first formal US payer-value review of the therapy and an early marker for the pricing debate.

news.headline: RTW Investments and Susquehanna disclose new stakes in uniQure in 13G filings
news.summary: RTW Investments reported a beneficial stake of roughly 3.94M shares (about 5.7%) and Susquehanna-affiliated entities disclosed a 3.34M-share (4.8%) position in filings accepted by the SEC on August 14. The disclosures pointed to continued institutional accumulation ahead of the BLA submission and the four-year AMT-130 data.

news.headline: Q2 2026 results: $810.3M cash funds operations into 2030; AMT-191 dosing paused on liver enzyme signal
news.summary: uniQure reported Q2 revenue of $5.8M (vs $5.3M a year earlier) and a net loss of $81.1M, or $1.22 per share, with cash and investments of $810.3M as of June 30 after the June equity raise of $259M gross at $45.50 per share - enough to fund the AMT-130 confirmatory trial and launch prep into 2030. On the pipeline, additional dosing in the AMT-191 Fabry study was paused pending evaluation of liver enzyme elevations in two mid-dose patients, while all 11 dosed patients had come off enzyme replacement therapy.

catalysts.label: Four-year AMT-130 Phase I/II data readout
catalysts.detail: uniQure has committed to presenting the four-year Phase I/II analysis before the end of Q3 2026, i.e. within the next three weeks, and reaffirmed that timing in the September 2 filing release. The dataset covers all 24 patients from the first two cohorts (12 high-dose, 12 low-dose) at four years plus additional high-dose patients at three years, from a June 30, 2026 data cut, benchmarked against the Enroll-HD natural-history database. With the BLA already filed, this is the single biggest near-term swing factor for the stock and no date has been announced yet, so it can land on any trading day in September.

catalysts.label: ICER scoping comment deadline
catalysts.detail: ICER's public comment period on the draft scoping document for its AMT-130 review closes September 11, 2026, with a revised scoping document expected on or about September 21. The framing set here shapes the value benchmark US payers will use against uniQure's eventual price for a one-time gene therapy.

catalysts.label: AMT-260 second-cohort enrollment completion
catalysts.detail: uniQure guided at Q2 results to completing enrollment of the second, higher-dose cohort (six patients) in the Phase I/IIa refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy study during Q3 2026, so confirmation is due by September 30. Full enrollment sets the clock for the H1 2027 data update and is the main visible progress marker in the non-AMT-130 pipeline this year.

catalysts.label: FDA filing decision and priority review determination
catalysts.detail: The FDA has a 60-day filing review period on the BLA submitted September 2, so acceptance for review should be communicated around early November 2026. The same decision point reveals whether priority review was granted - the difference between a six-month and a ten-month review clock and therefore between a Q2 2027 and a Q4 2027 potential approval. Acceptance also normally sets the PDUFA date. Sell-side views this acceptance as the next incremental de-risking event.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 results and regulatory update
catalysts.detail: uniQure's Q3 2026 print is expected around November 9-10, 2026 per consensus earnings-calendar estimates, not yet formally confirmed by the company. It is the first scheduled opportunity for management to confirm BLA acceptance, the review designation and PDUFA date, progress on the UK MAA, confirmatory-trial start-up and commercial build-out spending against the $810.3M cash position that funds operations into 2030.

catalysts.label: FDA advisory committee (AdCom) decision
catalysts.detail: Chief Medical Officer Walid Abi-Saab said in late July that the company considers an advisory committee meeting for what would be the first gene therapy for Huntington's disease probable and is preparing for one. The FDA has not confirmed a meeting or a date; timing would follow BLA acceptance rather than submission, so any announcement would most likely come with or after the filing decision expected in early November.

catalysts.label: Confirmatory trial initiation
catalysts.detail: uniQure and the FDA have aligned on the key design elements of the required confirmatory study: roughly 200 patients randomized 2:1 to AMT-130 versus standard of care, with Total Functional Capacity at 36 months as the primary endpoint. The company expects enrollment to be underway before the FDA's accelerated-approval decision, so a formal trial start announcement is a near-term operational milestone and a condition attached to any accelerated approval.

catalysts.label: Additional international regulatory pathways
catalysts.detail: uniQure has said it is pursuing further registration routes for AMT-130 beyond the US and UK, including EU options, and expected to give an update in the second half of 2026. The September 2 release covered only the FDA and MHRA submissions, so an EMA or other-jurisdiction filing plan remains outstanding. Any added jurisdiction expands the launch footprint beyond the roughly 30,000 diagnosed US patients.

catalysts.label: AMT-260 higher-dose epilepsy data and AMT-191 Fabry update
catalysts.detail: uniQure plans updated Phase I/IIa data in refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy in H1 2027, including the second, higher-dose cohort. First-cohort data in June 2026 showed 79-100% disabling-seizure reductions in three of six patients, with all adverse events mild or moderate and no immunosuppression required. A Fabry (AMT-191) update is guided to the same window, but dosing there is currently paused pending evaluation of liver enzyme elevations in two mid-dose patients. These are the only meaningful non-AMT-130 value drivers in the near pipeline.

catalysts.label: ICER evidence report and CEPAC verdict
catalysts.detail: ICER's draft evidence report on AMT-130 is due in January 2027, followed by a Midwest CEPAC public meeting in March 2027 where the panel deliberates and votes, and a final report in April 2027 - landing essentially on top of the expected FDA action date. The verdict frames the US pricing debate for a therapy expected to be priced in line with other one-time gene therapies.

catalysts.label: Potential FDA accelerated approval decision for AMT-130
catalysts.detail: With priority review granted, the FDA action date would land around late April or early May 2027, making AMT-130 potentially the first approved disease-modifying therapy for Huntington's disease. A US launch would follow into a market with no approved alternative after Roche's exit from the indication. Without priority review the decision slips toward late 2027.

catalysts.label: UK MHRA marketing authorisation decision
catalysts.detail: The MAA filed with the MHRA on September 2 runs on its own clock, independent of the FDA, and gives uniQure a second potential approval route plus first-mover position in a market with no disease-modifying Huntington's therapy. William Blair expects approval in both countries during 2027, but uniQure has not disclosed an expected MHRA decision timeline.

pulse: QURE closed the shortened pre-Labor-Day week around $44.50 for a market cap of roughly $3.1B, essentially flat over the past five sessions and about 38% below its $71.49 52-week high, even though the stock is still up more than 200% on the year with virtually the entire valuation resting on AMT-130. The long-awaited milestone landed and was sold: uniQure filed the US BLA for accelerated approval plus a parallel UK MAA on September 2 with a priority-review request, shares spiked to $50.74 intraday on September 3 and closed at $45.49, and no new company disclosure has followed in the days since, leaving a quiet tape against a consensus target near $70. The next three checkpoints in sequence are the still-undated four-year Phase I/II data uniQure has promised before September 30, the FDA's filing decision and priority-review answer expected around early November, and the still-unconfirmed advisory committee that would precede a potential approval around late April 2027.
